Two years ago, Sonos expanded from wireless speakers into the over-ear headphone space. Now, it seems Sonos is preparing to launch a more premium follow-up product that incorporates AI technology.

Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones are about to debut

Chris Welch reported for Bloomberg that Sonos is developing the Sonos Ace Ultra, as an upgraded successor to its 2024 Ace headphones.

An FCC application document exposed on Monday mentions the product name and shows up to five colour options, an increase from the original model's mere black and white.

Sonos plans to hold a product launch event in September. Based on the timeline of the application documents, the Ace Ultra could be one of the products unveiled at that event.

The application document also contains technical clues, suggesting the new headphones may support voice command functionality.

Bloomberg reported that CEO Tom Conrad acknowledged the original headphones lacked sufficient whole-home integration capabilities when launched, and showed no clear differentiation in the fiercely competitive market for similar products.

This time, Sonos appears to intend to combine its hardware more directly with its broader AI strategy.

Conrad has positioned the company's growth opportunity around conversational computing and predictive intelligence in the home environment, positioning Sonos devices as hardware that can operate across rooms and understand household living patterns.

The company has extended its Sonos voice control functionality to include operation of Philips Hue and Lutron Caseta.

Meanwhile, Apple's upgraded AirPods Max 2 launched in March, featuring an H2 chip, stronger noise cancellation, and real-time translation capabilities. Siri AI will extend to AirPods via iOS 27.

For more information on the upcoming Sonos Ace Ultra over-ear headphones, refer to Bloomberg's full report.
